n.quote:
To test the hypothesis that s(q, p) > s(p, q), we instructed two groups of 77
subjects each ... The two groups were presented with the same list of
21 pairs ... A t-test for correlated samples yielded t = 2 .92, df = 20, and
p < .01 . ... To obtain a statistical test based on individual data, we computed for
each subject a directional asymmetry score ... The average difference
(.42) was significantly positive : t = 2 .99, df = 153, p < .01 .

notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text begins with Studies of Similarity, Amos Tversky and Itamar Gati, Hebrew University, Jerusalem, and contains chapter pages 79–98 and primary experimental reporting. Title, authors, chapter pagination, Study 2 country stimuli and p. 87 match the neutral reference. The source header names the supplied DOI and a tvgati.pdf URL, but the body does not independently establish the 2024 reissue date or DOI. This is a primary chapter text, rather than an abstract, secondary article or preregistration; some OCR is clipped on p. 86. No PDF path was supplied, so no PDF rendering was possible. Only n_o is assigned; all other fields are unassigned placeholders. Target correspondence is unresolved: the locator identifies the Study 2 country similarity ratings, but p. 87 reports both a correlated-samples test across the 21 country pairs (t = 2 .92, df = 20, p < .01) and an individual directional-asymmetry test (t = 2 .99, df = 153, p < .01). Candidate analytic units: 21 country pairs for the former; 77 + 77 = 154 participants in two distinct presentation-order groups for the latter. This participant sum is based on explicit group sizes, not degrees of freedom, and is retained only as a candidate. The 68 prominence-validation subjects, 69 statement-preference subjects on p. 86, and two groups of 23 difference-rating subjects on p. 87 belong to different tasks and are excluded from these candidates. The chapter notes on p. 84 that problem-level response counts could be smaller than total subjects; no specific exclusions are stated for the individual asymmetry test. No candidate was selected by input order, audit identifier or numerical matching.
